quest.title: The Last Day of Remuria
quest.description: After learning the true identity of "Monsieur Os," you decide to go to the Sea of Bygone Eras to track down Boethius...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x250, Primogem x30, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x2

talks.objective: Head to the Sea of Bygone Eras
Head to the Sea of Bygone Eras

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, those examples weren't very convincing, were they...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: C—C'mon, Osse, no amount of suspicious looks is going to suddenly give us better options!

dialogues.speaker: Monsieur Os
dialogues.text: *sigh* I know. You're right. Let's give it a try.

dialogues.speaker: Monsieur Os
dialogues.text: The seals that bind the evil dragon seem to be connected to three locations. Let us begin by removing the chains in those three places.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's go.

talks.objective: Break the chains that bind Scylla

dialogues.speaker: Scylla
dialogues.text: All ready, little ones?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I need a moment to prep...

dialogues.speaker: Scylla
dialogues.text: Of course. Gird yourself sufficiently, and then, let us go. I shall wait for you below.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I need a moment to prep...

dialogues.speaker: Scylla
dialogues.text: Of course. Gird yourself sufficiently, and then, let us go.

talks.objective: Pass through the Initium Iani with Scylla

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... Looks just like that glowing fish we saw before!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There are still weird things tangled around the top nearby... What the heck is going on? Paimon's getting more and more confused...

choices.text: I've heard this voice in a dream before...

response.speaker: Monsieur Os
response.text: Yes, you must have met him in the Sebastos's dream, did you not?

response.speaker: Monsieur Os
response.text: Scylla, a fell dragon who once served the Sebastos. He was subdued and sealed here by Boethius.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ehh!? Mr. Super Rude subdued an evil dragon? Paimon didn't think he could do something that amazing...

response.speaker: Monsieur Os
response.text: Well, "fell dragon" was the name they gave, but it was no more than a vishap that was a teensy bit stronger than normal. After all, no new Hydro Dragon could be born so long as the Mistress of Many Waters hibernated in the deep seas.

choices.text: I can't remember his name anymore, though...

dialogues.speaker: Scylla
dialogues.text: Ahhh! Such warm ocean currents! Free at last!

dialogues.speaker: Scylla
dialogues.text: Well now, little ones. Hail you from the surface? I know not for what reason you have come to this deepwater prison, but...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We aren't "little" anything! You're just way too big!

dialogues.speaker: Scylla
dialogues.text: Haha! Very well! Either way, you have broken the shackles that have bound me for millennia. That places me in your debt.

dialogues.speaker: Scylla
dialogues.text: If there is any undertaking in which I may aid you, then speak. Consider it a token of my gratitude.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hehe, Paimon knew you'd be a reasonable guy! Anyway, Paimon's name is Paimon, and {M#he's}{F#she's} {NICKNAME}. And this is...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Err, actually, Paimon's not sure what you'd know him by, but we call him Monsieur Os!

dialogues.speaker: Scylla
dialogues.text: Ah, Cassiodor, it is you. It has been a while. So you came back after all. But still, you are sadly late... by a few thousand years, no less.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, looks like the big guy knows you, Monsieur Os!

dialogues.speaker: Monsieur Os
dialogues.text: I have nothing to say to despicable traitors.

dialogues.speaker: Scylla
dialogues.text: Speak not so rashly, mortal! We are dragon-born. We keep all our promises and betray none, which is more than can be said for your haughty race.

dialogues.speaker: Monsieur Os
dialogues.text: Save your breath! It is worth less than a drowning mayfly! Your betrayal is undisputed. Were we not defeated in that war precisely because you turned against us?

dialogues.speaker: Monsieur Os
dialogues.text: If we hadn't lost that war... our nation... the Sebastos... wouldn't have...

dialogues.speaker: Scylla
dialogues.text: Ah, you've been gone far too long, Cassiodor! The truth is not what you imagine... Though I suppose that a secret plan would not have been secret had its details reached your ears.

dialogues.speaker: Monsieur Os
dialogues.text: ...Secret plan?

dialogues.speaker: Scylla
dialogues.text: My leading an army of vishaps to assault the capital was, in fact, part of Remus's final, secret plan.

dialogues.speaker: Scylla
dialogues.text: And he did all this to save his nation and people — a man of great moral character.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, that is kinda weird. Why would a ruler ask someone else to invade their own country?

response.speaker: Scylla
response.text: And what, little one, would ones such as you or I know of Remus's thoughts? Whatever the case, look upon this, Cassiodor. Even you should be able to divine its meaning.

response.speaker: Monsieur Os
response.text: The guiding golden bees... They should only heed the call of the Symphony... Why would the Sebastos bestow his power upon a savage dragon?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Because they had an arrangement...

response.speaker: Scylla
response.text: Oh? You know much, little one! From where did you learn that?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: From memories scattered in the sea...

response.speaker: Scylla
response.text: You speak correctly! Yes, indeed, we did have an arrangement, but I failed him. I squandered his noble sacrifice.

response.speaker: Scylla
response.text: I could not make it to Domus Aurea in time! And so the waves devoured the whole city, and my kindred could not escape, either...

response.speaker: Monsieur Os
response.text: ...How could such a thing be...

response.speaker: Scylla
response.text: Hmph! If it is betrayal you speak of, then Boethius was the true traitor!

response.speaker: Scylla
response.text: Were it not for that lying devil, that deceitful rat, and his silver-tongued deceptions, how could a prince among dragon-kin such as I, who once led our armies after the age of the ancient dragons, have been beaten so easily?

response.speaker: Scylla
response.text: That devil first falsely claimed to have given up resistance on Remus's orders, saying he had ordered the legions to cease resistance. Yet when we arrived here, he suddenly rose up against us...

response.speaker: Scylla
response.text: Now that I have had much time to think on it, I fear he must have learned of Remus's plans somehow, and thus was able to set up such an inescapable trap and lure me in, step by step...

response.speaker: Scylla
response.text: And thus did my flesh and blood turn to stone, and thus did it remain for millennia, to this day, when you rescued me.

response.speaker: Monsieur Os
response.text: Boethius knew perfectly well what a massive calamity his actions would bring about, yet he still... Could he have been trying to seize control over Phobos? Was that why he committed such sins...?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It seems that we don't have the full story yet...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So the guy who keeps calling others traitors was actually a traitor through and through!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But why, though? Ugh, are we gonna have to ask him? Paimon doubts we'd get a straight answer.

response.speaker: Scylla
response.text: Hmm? So that loathsome, recalcitrant demon-worm has yet to dissipate, has he?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, and he's stolen the souls of a whole bunch of Fontainians, too! Rescuing them is actually the main reason we're here...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He said that he'd wait for us within Domus Aurea... Well, he just said he'd wait for Monsieur Os, so we're coming along uninvited!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Not even leaving a door, though. How rude of him!

response.speaker: Scylla
response.text: The Initium Iani...? Hmph, though feeble tricks and smokescreens have been set to dismay us, but at the end of the day, it's nothing more than a glorified stone door.

response.speaker: Scylla
response.text: I may have lost my physical body, but it is no great labor to take the little ones over to settle the matter.

response.speaker: Scylla
response.text: Watch closely, little ones!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oooh! You're pretty reliable, huh, big guy?

response.speaker: Scylla
response.text: Now we simply need to break these revealed seals one by one. If you are prepared, then let us go!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well then, Monsieur Os, are you ready?

response.speaker: Monsieur Os
response.text: Now that it's come to this, we have little choice.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Alright then. What about you, {NICKNAME}? Ready?

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: You go back to the outer face of the Initium Iani...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I never thought that vishaps could get this large.

dialogues.speaker: Monsieur Os
dialogues.text: Hmph. After all, they are little more than uncultured barbarians. It would be unsurprising if they grew into something much stranger.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, isn't Neuvillette...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right! Neuvillette's the Hydro Dragon, isn't he? That doesn't mean that this guy's way older than even him, does it?

dialogues.speaker: Monsieur Os
dialogues.text: A new Dragon of Water has already been born? Then again, it has been a long time since even the former Mistress of Many Waters passed... So much time has passed...

dialogues.speaker: Monsieur Os
dialogues.text: In any case, the evil dragon Scylla was once the Sebastos's friend, but he revolted at a critical juncture in the showdown between us Remurians and the... Fontainians.

dialogues.speaker: Monsieur Os
dialogues.text: At that time, Scylla led the brutal Dragonborn to Machimos, intent on breaching the inner city, Capitolium, where the Sebastos resided.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, the people in town were always talking about some Machimos, and a belltower or something...

response.speaker: Monsieur Os
response.text: Correct. "Machimos" is the outer city of the capital, but should the fell dragon wish to enter the inner city, he must pass through the Initium Iani.

response.speaker: Monsieur Os
response.text: That is the barrier separating the inner and outer parts of the capital, and the Symphony weaved by the Sebastos and the musicians which covered all of Remuria passed through the Initium Iani and its golden waterways.

response.speaker: Monsieur Os
response.text: Boethius and his legions used this fact to shut the Initium Iani, thus finally sealing the evil dragon.

response.speaker: Monsieur Os
response.text: Perhaps Scylla sought to go before the Sebastos's throne, but such an opportunity is now forever lost. Afterward, the evil dragon sank alongside Remuria, and the Sebastos too was lost, remaining so to this very day...

response.speaker: Monsieur Os
response.text: #Did you recall something, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It all feels a bit muddled...

response.speaker: Monsieur Os
response.text: That is true... I only heard tell of events after it had all transpired myself, having not been in the capital when the disaster struck...

response.speaker: Monsieur Os
response.text: Then, none knew just what had happened to the Sebastos. I fear that we can only learn more by proceeding further.

response.speaker: Monsieur Os
response.text: The large glowing fish that we saw in the castle must be the thoughts that escaped from fissures in Scylla's stony cell.

response.speaker: Monsieur Os
response.text: I fear he has already taken notice of our presence. Having been sealed here for so long, now that he's finally sensed outsiders, he will naturally find a way to lure us in.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that's it...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hang on a minute! You said that the way to Domus Aurea is through those gates or something, but hasn't Boethius shut them already? Doesn't this mean there's no getting through?

response.speaker: Monsieur Os
response.text: This will prove quite tricky, yes...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Bah, there's gotta be a limit to how rude you can be! What's with this "I'll wait for you at Domus Aurea, mwahaha!" nonsense when you won't even leave the door open, huh!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Y'know, why don't we find some way to break the seal on the evil dragon, and get the former foe he beat to break the door down for us?

response.speaker: Monsieur Os
response.text: No! How could we do such a thing!? I mean, after all, that is one of Remuria's nemeses...

choices.text: But the enemy of my enemy is my friend, no?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right. It's been so long. For all you know, he might've decided to turn over a new leaf and be a nice dragon!

response.speaker: Monsieur Os
response.text: But he is still a dragon...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Eh, come on, so what? Even if he is a dragon, he might be the reasonable kind we can talk with. We've got experience in dealing with dragons, don't we, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: But Remuria is long gone, no?
(Scylla should have come and seen Remus before...)
I heard people talking about that in town.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, there was that time with Dvalin...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yup, that bit where he kicked up a storm in Mondstadt while under the influence of a curse. We had a big fight because of it, too...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We had that little run-in with Azhdaha...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right, he was trying to break that seal, so we teamed up with everyone and had to beat him together before we could reseal him...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We encountered Apep in the desert...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right, she even went on about wanting to destroy Sumeru... And then we had to defeat the anomalous lifeforms within her before we managed to get her healthy again...
